verdicts.flaw_description: A rival cause reaches every unit: 'Each shop moved its machines to a coated carbide insert grade that quarter, and every logged run was cut on one of those machines.' A new insert grade shortens cycle time on its own, so the 4-7 minute reductions cannot be attributed to the coolant.

Two of the four cases have the outcome measured before the kit was issued: case One is 'issued 4 November; by 27 September' and case Three is 'issued 5 June; by 28 April'. The gain in those sections predates the exposure.

The measured population is narrower than the claim: 'Figures cover the orders rung up at the new prices, and about a fifth of each line's orders were rung up at the old prices.' A self-selected 80% of current orders is compared against the whole line a month earlier, so the 4-7 percent gain need not hold for revenue per order overall.

The timings exclude the runs most likely to be slow: 'Timings cover the runs that stayed on the issued route, and about a sixth of each depot's runs left the issued route.' That compliant subset is compared to all runs a month earlier, so the 5-9 minute saving is a selection artefact as much as a routing effect.

The absence figures drop part of the cohort: 'Absence figures cover the pupils on the revised timetable throughout, and about a fifth of each cohort spent weeks on the old timetable.' Excluding the fifth who came off the timetable (plausibly the more absent pupils) while comparing to the full cohort a term earlier cannot establish an absence reduction for the cohort.
